block.title: Hello’s library refactor cuts the time to open a proof
block.p: Removing the functors from Hello’s library proofs cut the time to open hello_libs by half on swa. The safety and locale proofs also open faster because they import the same library.

Each time below is the median wall time of six rq open commands with compiled interfaces on disk. Each command started a fresh worker and stopped at the named proof. The runs alternated revision order and used Rocq 9.3 on both revisions.

Before the change, Rocq spent 1.33 s processing module declarations on the way to hello_libs. Removing those declarations accounts for most of the saving. The median peak memory of that worker fell from 1,183 MiB to 666 MiB.

The OS-world proof in the last row has no Hello imports. A one-line edit inside an open safety proof took 0.51 s to reload on each revision. The worker reused the preceding sentences in all twelve reloads.
With an empty interface cache and twelve build jobs, the first open of the safety theorem took 171 s before the change and 159 s after it. Each revision had one such run.
